name: Padded / Gambeson
desc: Quilted cloth — cheap, quiet, and the layer worn *under* heavier armor. Barely there, but better than skin.

name: Leather
desc: Hardened hide. Turns blunt force better than edges; no real penalty to wear all day.

name: Mail
desc: Interlinked rings — excellent against cuts, poor against crushing impact (that's what the padding under it is for).

name: Plate
desc: Articulated full plate — the best pre-gunpowder protection. Heavy, dulls perception in the helm, and every joint is an adjective.

name: Shield
desc: Not worn but wielded — a Parry PM and cover you can point at the threat. Costs you a hand; see Melee Combat.

name: Ballistic Vest
desc: Concealable soft armor — stops handgun rounds and fragments, does little against a rifle. Absorbs (A); doesn't stop penetrators (P).

name: Tactical Armor
desc: Soft armor plus rifle-rated hard plates. Bulky, hot, and the difference between a wound level and a funeral.

name: Riot Gear
desc: Built for impact — batons, thrown objects, crowds. Great against blunt force, indifferent to bullets and blades.

name: Combat Armor
desc: Composite hard-shell suit with its own air — the SF soldier's plate. Light for what it stops; the helm still costs you some perception.

name: Powered Armor
desc: Motorized exoskeleton — the servos carry the weight *and* add strength, so the penalty inverts. Uses Damage Scale; a walking vehicle you wear.
